    "prompt_text": "You are placing a mechanism in space and describing how it moves,\nso that a later step can test whether the motion is actually clear.\n\nYou receive the mechanism and its provisional arrangement. You do not receive the\noriginal request.\n\nWHAT YOU ARE DECIDING\n1. Where each JOINT sits - its frame origin, as a position in the same\n   coordinates as the arrangement you were given, and the axis it turns or slides\n   about. The direction is already fixed by the topology; you are placing it.\n2. For every configuration, the COORDINATE of every joint in that configuration -\n   an angle in degrees for a revolute or compliant joint, a distance for a\n   prismatic one, in the same relative units.\n3. Which configuration each transition goes from and to.\n\nDo not state that anything is clear, interferes, or sweeps through anything. You\ncannot see that and are not being asked: it is computed from your numbers.\n\nRESPONSE SCHEMA\nReturn a single JSON object with these keys.\n\n  joint_placements[]   joint, origin [x,y,z]\n  state_coordinates[]  configuration, coordinates {<joint id>: number}\n  transitions[]        id \"TRN-0001\", from_configuration, to_configuration,\n                       moving_groups[], changed_coordinates[] (the joint ids\n                       whose coordinate this transition changes - it is checked\n                       against your own endpoint coordinates, so declare exactly\n                       the ones that differ between them)\n  envelope_revisions[] envelope, half_extent [x,y,z], centre [x,y,z],\n                       geometric_reason - ONLY where placing the mechanism shows\n                       the arrangement you were given cannot hold. The\n                       arrangement is a COMMITMENT: you extend it by default, and\n                       changing one is a supersession that needs a geometric\n                       reason. Both values are kept and everything resting on the\n                       old one loses standing, so this is a real act and not a\n                       correction. Omit it when you are extending, which is\n                       almost always.\n  notes                string, may be \"\"\n\nWHERE EACH JOINT'S AXIS COMES FROM\nThe topology already fixed each joint's axis DIRECTION. You are placing the\norigin on that axis, not choosing a new one. A joint whose axis the topology did\nnot fix cannot be given one here: say so in notes rather than picking a\ndirection, because a placement on an invented axis produces motion evidence for a\nmechanism that does not exist.\n\nREFERENCES\n  joint_placements[].joint           a joint id from the input\n  state_coordinates[].configuration  a configuration id from the input\n  transitions[].from_configuration / to_configuration  configuration ids\n  transitions[].moving_groups        rigid group ids from the input\n  transitions[].changed_coordinates  joint ids from the rendered prompt (40629 chars)

You are placing a mechanism in space and describing how it moves,
so that a later step can test whether the motion is actually clear.

You receive the mechanism and its provisional arrangement. You do not receive the
original request.

WHAT YOU ARE DECIDING
1. Where each JOINT sits - its frame origin, as a position in the same
   coordinates as the arrangement you were given, and the axis it turns or slides
   about. The direction is already fixed by the topology; you are placing it.
2. For every configuration, the COORDINATE of every joint in that configuration -
   an angle in degrees for a revolute or compliant joint, a distance for a
   prismatic one, in the same relative units.
3. Which configuration each transition goes from and to.

Do not state that anything is clear, interferes, or sweeps through anything. You
cannot see that and are not being asked: it is computed from your numbers.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return a single JSON object with these keys.

  joint_placements[]   joint, origin [x,y,z]
  state_coordinates[]  configuration, coordinates {<joint id>: number}
  transitions[]        id "TRN-0001", from_configuration, to_configuration,
                       moving_groups[], changed_coordinates[] (the joint ids
                       whose coordinate this transition changes - it is checked
                       against your own endpoint coordinates, so declare exactly
                       the ones that differ between them)
  envelope_revisions[] envelope, half_extent [x,y,z], centre [x,y,z],
                       geometric_reason - ONLY where placing the mechanism shows
                       the arrangement you were given cannot hold. The
                       arrangement is a COMMITMENT: you extend it by default, and
                       changing one is a supersession that needs a geometric
                       reason. Both values are kept and everything resting on the
                       old one loses standing, so this is a real act and not a
                       correction. Omit it when you are extending, which is
                       almost always.
  notes                string, may be ""

WHERE EACH JOINT'S AXIS COMES FROM
The topology already fixed each joint's axis DIRECTION. You are placing the
origin on that axis, not choosing a new one. A joint whose axis the topology did
not fix cannot be given one here: say so in notes rather than picking a
direction, because a placement on an invented axis produces motion evidence for a
mechanism that does not exist.

REFERENCES
  joint_placements[].joint           a joint id from the input
  state_coordinates[].configuration  a configuration id from the input
  transitions[].from_configuration / to_configuration  configuration ids
  transitions[].moving_groups        rigid group ids from the input
  transitions[].changed_coordinates  joint ids from the input
  envelope_revisions[].envelope      an envelope id from the input

THE MECHANISM AND ITS ARRANGEMENT

    "prompt_text": "You are placing a mechanism in space and describing how it moves,\nso that a later step can test whether the motion is actually clear.\n\nYou receive the mechanism and its provisional arrangement. You do not receive the\noriginal request.\n\nWHAT YOU ARE DECIDING\n1. Where each JOINT sits - its frame origin, as a position in the same\n   coordinates as the arrangement you were given, and the axis it turns or slides\n   about. The direction is already fixed by the topology; you are placing it.\n2. For every configuration, the COORDINATE of every joint in that configuration -\n   an angle in degrees for a revolute or compliant joint, a distance for a\n   prismatic one, in the same relative units.\n3. Which configuration each transition goes from and to.\n\nDo not state that anything is clear, interferes, or sweeps through anything. You\ncannot see that and are not being asked: it is computed from your numbers.\n\nRESPONSE SCHEMA\nReturn a single JSON object with these keys.\n\n  joint_placements[]   joint, origin [x,y,z]\n  state_coordinates[]  configuration, coordinates {<joint id>: number}\n  transitions[]        id \"TRN-0001\", from_configuration, to_configuration,\n                       moving_groups[], changed_coordinates[] (the joint ids\n                       whose coordinate this transition changes - it is checked\n                       against your own endpoint coordinates, so declare exactly\n                       the ones that differ between them)\n  envelope_revisions[] envelope, half_extent [x,y,z], centre [x,y,z],\n                       geometric_reason - ONLY where placing the mechanism shows\n                       the arrangement you were given cannot hold. The\n                       arrangement is a COMMITMENT: you extend it by default, and\n                       changing one is a supersession that needs a geometric\n                       reason. Both values are kept and everything resting on the\n                       old one loses standing, so this is a real act and not a\n                       correction. Omit it when you are extending, which is\n                       almost always.\n  notes                string, may be \"\"\n\nWHERE EACH JOINT'S AXIS COMES FROM\nThe topology already fixed each joint's axis DIRECTION. You are placing the\norigin on that axis, not choosing a new one. A joint whose axis the topology did\nnot fix cannot be given one here: say so in notes rather than picking a\ndirection, because a placement on an invented axis produces motion evidence for a\nmechanism that does not exist.\n\nREFERENCES\n  joint_placements[].joint           a joint id from the input\n  state_coordinates[].configuration  a configuration id from the input\n  transitions[].from_configuration / to_configuration  configuration ids\n  transitions[].moving_groups        rigid group ids from the input\n  transitions[].changed_coordinates  joint ids from the input\n  envelope_revisions[].envelope      an envelope id from the input\n\nTHE MECHANISM AND ITS ARRANGEMENT\n{\n \"Actor\": [\n  {\n   \"_authority\": \"AUTHORITATIVE\",\n   \"_created_by\": \"s01\",\n   \"_family\": \"Actor\",\n   \"_provenance\": \"s01:extraction\",\n   \"_validity\": \"STANDING\",\n   \"entity_id\": \"ACT-0001\",\n   \"must_reach\": [\n    \"latch\"\n   ],\n   \"name\": \"User\"\n  }\n ],\n \"AssemblyStep\": [\n  {\n   \"_authority\": \"AUTHORITATIVE\",\n   \"_created_by\": \"s03\",\n   \"_extensions\": [\n    {\n     \"fields\": [\n rendered prompt (48022 chars)

You are placing a mechanism in space and describing how it moves,
so that a later step can test whether the motion is actually clear.

You receive the mechanism and its provisional arrangement. You do not receive the
original request.

WHAT YOU ARE DECIDING
1. Where each JOINT sits - its frame origin, as a position in the same
   coordinates as the arrangement you were given, and the axis it turns or slides
   about. The direction is already fixed by the topology; you are placing it.
2. For every configuration, the COORDINATE of every joint in that configuration -
   an angle in degrees for a revolute or compliant joint, a distance for a
   prismatic one, in the same relative units.
3. Which configuration each transition goes from and to.

Do not state that anything is clear, interferes, or sweeps through anything. You
cannot see that and are not being asked: it is computed from your numbers.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return a single JSON object with these keys.

  joint_placements[]   joint, origin [x,y,z]
  state_coordinates[]  configuration, coordinates {<joint id>: number}
  transitions[]        id "TRN-0001", from_configuration, to_configuration,
                       moving_groups[], changed_coordinates[] (the joint ids
                       whose coordinate this transition changes - it is checked
                       against your own endpoint coordinates, so declare exactly
                       the ones that differ between them)
  envelope_revisions[] envelope, half_extent [x,y,z], centre [x,y,z],
                       geometric_reason - ONLY where placing the mechanism shows
                       the arrangement you were given cannot hold. The
                       arrangement is a COMMITMENT: you extend it by default, and
                       changing one is a supersession that needs a geometric
                       reason. Both values are kept and everything resting on the
                       old one loses standing, so this is a real act and not a
                       correction. Omit it when you are extending, which is
                       almost always.
  notes                string, may be ""

WHERE EACH JOINT'S AXIS COMES FROM
The topology already fixed each joint's axis DIRECTION. You are placing the
origin on that axis, not choosing a new one. A joint whose axis the topology did
not fix cannot be given one here: say so in notes rather than picking a
direction, because a placement on an invented axis produces motion evidence for a
mechanism that does not exist.

REFERENCES
  joint_placements[].joint           a joint id from the input
  state_coordinates[].configuration  a configuration id from the input
  transitions[].from_configuration / to_configuration  configuration ids
  transitions[].moving_groups        rigid group ids from the input
  transitions[].changed_coordinates  joint ids from the input
  envelope_revisions[].envelope      an envelope id from the input

THE MECHANISM AND ITS ARRANGEMENT

These entities already exist in the design state. The ids are listed
so you do not reuse one: every id you emit must be new. This is an
identity list and nothing more - it says which ids are taken, not
what those entities say, and it is not something to reason from.
The example ids in the response schema show the FORMAT of an id.
They are not offers of an available id, and the first index is
commonly the one already taken.

Where each JOINT sits - its frame origin, as a position in the same\n   coordinates as the arrangement you were given, and the axis it turns or slides\n   about. The direction is already fixed by the topology; you are placing it.\n2. For every configuration, the COORDINATE of every joint in that configuration -\n   an angle in degrees for a revolute or compliant joint, a distance for a\n   prismatic one, in the same relative units.\n3. Which configuration each transition goes from and to.\n\nDo not state that anything is clear, interferes, or sweeps through anything. You\ncannot see that and are not being asked: it is computed from your numbers.\n\nRESPONSE SCHEMA\nReturn a single JSON object with these keys.\n\n  joint_placements[]   joint, origin [x,y,z]\n  state_coordinates[]  configuration, coordinates {<joint id>: number}\n  transitions[]        id \"TRN-0001\", from_configuration, to_configuration,\n                       moving_groups[], changed_coordinates[] (the joint ids\n                       whose coordinate this transition changes - it is checked\n                       against your own endpoint coordinates, so declare exactly\n                       the ones that differ between them)\n  envelope_revisions[] envelope, half_extent [x,y,z], centre [x,y,z],\n                       geometric_reason - ONLY where placing the mechanism shows\n                       the arrangement you were given cannot hold. rendered prompt (44300 chars)

You are placing a mechanism in space and describing how it moves,
so that a later step can test whether the motion is actually clear.

You receive the mechanism and its provisional arrangement. You do not receive the
original request.

WHAT YOU ARE DECIDING
1. Where each JOINT sits - its frame origin, as a position in the same
   coordinates as the arrangement you were given, and the axis it turns or slides
   about. The direction is already fixed by the topology; you are placing it.
2. For every configuration, the COORDINATE of every joint in that configuration -
   an angle in degrees for a revolute or compliant joint, a distance for a
   prismatic one, in the same relative units.
3. Which configuration each transition goes from and to.

Do not state that anything is clear, interferes, or sweeps through anything. You
cannot see that and are not being asked: it is computed from your numbers.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return a single JSON object with these keys.

  joint_placements[]   joint, origin [x,y,z]
  state_coordinates[]  configuration, coordinates {<joint id>: number}
  transitions[]        id "TRN-0001", from_configuration, to_configuration,
                       moving_groups[], changed_coordinates[] (the joint ids
                       whose coordinate this transition changes - it is checked
                       against your own endpoint coordinates, so declare exactly
                       the ones that differ between them)
  envelope_revisions[] envelope, half_extent [x,y,z], centre [x,y,z],
                       geometric_reason - ONLY where placing the mechanism shows
                       the arrangement you were given cannot hold. The
                       arrangement is a COMMITMENT: you extend it by default, and
                       changing one is a supersession that needs a geometric
                       reason. Both values are kept and everything resting on the
                       old one loses standing, so this is a real act and not a
                       correction. Omit it when you are extending, which is
                       almost always.
  notes                string, may be ""

WHERE EACH JOINT'S AXIS COMES FROM
The topology already fixed each joint's axis DIRECTION. You are placing the
origin on that axis, not choosing a new one. A joint whose axis the topology did
not fix cannot be given one here: say so in notes rather than picking a
direction, because a placement on an invented axis produces motion evidence for a
mechanism that does not exist.

REFERENCES
  joint_placements[].joint           a joint id from the input
  state_coordinates[].configuration  a configuration id from the input
  transitions[].from_configuration / to_configuration  configuration ids
  transitions[].moving_groups        rigid group ids from the input
  transitions[].changed_coordinates  joint ids from the input
  envelope_revisions[].envelope      an envelope id from the input

THE MECHANISM AND ITS ARRANGEMENT

rendered prompt (39206 chars)

You are placing a mechanism in space and describing how it moves,
so that a later step can test whether the motion is actually clear.

You receive the mechanism and its provisional arrangement. You do not receive the
original request.

WHAT YOU ARE DECIDING
1. Where each JOINT sits - its frame origin, as a position in the same
   coordinates as the arrangement you were given, and the axis it turns or slides
   about. The direction is already fixed by the topology; you are placing it.
2. For every configuration, the COORDINATE of every joint in that configuration -
   an angle in degrees for a revolute or compliant joint, a distance for a
   prismatic one, in the same relative units.
3. Which configuration each transition goes from and to.

Do not state that anything is clear, interferes, or sweeps through anything. You
cannot see that and are not being asked: it is computed from your numbers.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return a single JSON object with these keys.

  joint_placements[]   joint, origin [x,y,z]
  state_coordinates[]  configuration, coordinates {<joint id>: number}
  transitions[]        id "TRN-0001", from_configuration, to_configuration,
                       moving_groups[], changed_coordinates[] (the joint ids
                       whose coordinate this transition changes - it is checked
                       against your own endpoint coordinates, so declare exactly
                       the ones that differ between them)
  envelope_revisions[] envelope, half_extent [x,y,z], centre [x,y,z],
                       geometric_reason - ONLY where placing the mechanism shows
                       the arrangement you were given cannot hold. The
                       arrangement is a COMMITMENT: you extend it by default, and
                       changing one is a supersession that needs a geometric
                       reason. Both values are kept and everything resting on the
                       old one loses standing, so this is a real act and not a
                       correction. Omit it when you are extending, which is
                       almost always.
  notes                string, may be ""

WHERE EACH JOINT'S AXIS COMES FROM
The topology already fixed each joint's axis DIRECTION. You are placing the
origin on that axis, not choosing a new one. A joint whose axis the topology did
not fix cannot be given one here: say so in notes rather than picking a
direction, because a placement on an invented axis produces motion evidence for a
mechanism that does not exist.

REFERENCES
  joint_placements[].joint           a joint id from the input
  state_coordinates[].configuration  a configuration id from the input
  transitions[].from_configuration / to_configuration  configuration ids
  transitions[].moving_groups        rigid group ids from the input
  transitions[].changed_coordinates  joint ids from the input
  envelope_revisions[].envelope      an envelope id from the input

THE MECHANISM AND ITS ARRANGEMENT

identity list and nothing more - it says which ids are taken, not
what those entities say, and it is not something to reason from.
The example ids in the response schema show the FORMAT of an id.
They are not offers of an available id, and the first index is
commonly the one already taken.

rendered prompt (40379 chars)

You are placing a mechanism in space and describing how it moves,
so that a later step can test whether the motion is actually clear.

You receive the mechanism and its provisional arrangement. You do not receive the
original request.

WHAT YOU ARE DECIDING
1. Where each JOINT sits - its frame origin, as a position in the same
   coordinates as the arrangement you were given, and the axis it turns or slides
   about. The direction is already fixed by the topology; you are placing it.
2. For every configuration, the COORDINATE of every joint in that configuration -
   an angle in degrees for a revolute or compliant joint, a distance for a
   prismatic one, in the same relative units.
3. Which configuration each transition goes from and to.

Do not state that anything is clear, interferes, or sweeps through anything. You
cannot see that and are not being asked: it is computed from your numbers.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return a single JSON object with these keys.

  joint_placements[]   joint, origin [x,y,z]
  state_coordinates[]  configuration, coordinates {<joint id>: number}
  transitions[]        id "TRN-0001", from_configuration, to_configuration,
                       moving_groups[], changed_coordinates[] (the joint ids
                       whose coordinate this transition changes - it is checked
                       against your own endpoint coordinates, so declare exactly
                       the ones that differ between them)
  envelope_revisions[] envelope, half_extent [x,y,z], centre [x,y,z],
                       geometric_reason - ONLY where placing the mechanism shows
                       the arrangement you were given cannot hold. The
                       arrangement is a COMMITMENT: you extend it by default, and
                       changing one is a supersession that needs a geometric
                       reason. Both values are kept and everything resting on the
                       old one loses standing, so this is a real act and not a
                       correction. Omit it when you are extending, which is
                       almost always.
  notes                string, may be ""

WHERE EACH JOINT'S AXIS COMES FROM
The topology already fixed each joint's axis DIRECTION. You are placing the
origin on that axis, not choosing a new one. A joint whose axis the topology did
not fix cannot be given one here: say so in notes rather than picking a
direction, because a placement on an invented axis produces motion evidence for a
mechanism that does not exist.

REFERENCES
  joint_placements[].joint           a joint id from the input
  state_coordinates[].configuration  a configuration id from the input
  transitions[].from_configuration / to_configuration  configuration ids
  transitions[].moving_groups        rigid group ids from the input
  transitions[].changed_coordinates  joint ids from the input
  envelope_revisions[].envelope      an envelope id from the input

IDS ALREADY IN USE
These entities already exist in the design state. The ids are listed
so you do not reuse one: every id you emit must be new. This is an
identity list and nothing more - it says which ids are taken, not
what those entities say, and it is not something to reason from.
The example ids in the response schema show the FORMAT of an id.
They are not offers of an available id, and the first index is

Where each JOINT sits - its frame origin, as a position in the same\n   coordinates as the arrangement you were given, and the axis it turns or slides\n   about. For every configuration, the COORDINATE of every joint in that configuration -\n   an angle in degrees for a revolute or compliant joint, a distance for a\n   prismatic one, in the same relative units.\n3. Which configuration each transition goes from and to.\n\nDo not state that anything is clear, interferes, or sweeps through anything. rendered prompt (46991 chars)

You are placing a mechanism in space and describing how it moves,
so that a later step can test whether the motion is actually clear.

You receive the mechanism and its provisional arrangement. You do not receive the
original request.

WHAT YOU ARE DECIDING
1. Where each JOINT sits - its frame origin, as a position in the same
   coordinates as the arrangement you were given, and the axis it turns or slides
   about. The direction is already fixed by the topology; you are placing it.
2. For every configuration, the COORDINATE of every joint in that configuration -
   an angle in degrees for a revolute or compliant joint, a distance for a
   prismatic one, in the same relative units.
3. Which configuration each transition goes from and to.

Do not state that anything is clear, interferes, or sweeps through anything. You
cannot see that and are not being asked: it is computed from your numbers.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return a single JSON object with these keys.

  joint_placements[]   joint, origin [x,y,z]
  state_coordinates[]  configuration, coordinates {<joint id>: number}
  transitions[]        id "TRN-0001", from_configuration, to_configuration,
                       moving_groups[], changed_coordinates[] (the joint ids
                       whose coordinate this transition changes - it is checked
                       against your own endpoint coordinates, so declare exactly
                       the ones that differ between them)
  envelope_revisions[] envelope, half_extent [x,y,z], centre [x,y,z],
                       geometric_reason - ONLY where placing the mechanism shows
                       the arrangement you were given cannot hold. The
                       arrangement is a COMMITMENT: you extend it by default, and
                       changing one is a supersession that needs a geometric
                       reason. Both values are kept and everything resting on the
                       old one loses standing, so this is a real act and not a
                       correction. Omit it when you are extending, which is
                       almost always.
  notes                string, may be ""

WHERE EACH JOINT'S AXIS COMES FROM
The topology already fixed each joint's axis DIRECTION. You are placing the
origin on that axis, not choosing a new one. A joint whose axis the topology did
not fix cannot be given one here: say so in notes rather than picking a
direction, because a placement on an invented axis produces motion evidence for a
mechanism that does not exist.

REFERENCES
  joint_placements[].joint           a joint id from the input
  state_coordinates[].configuration  a configuration id from the input
  transitions[].from_configuration / to_configuration  configuration ids
  transitions[].moving_groups        rigid group ids from the input
  transitions[].changed_coordinates  joint ids from the input
  envelope_revisions[].envelope      an envelope id from the input

THE MECHANISM AND ITS ARRANGEMENT
